summary: Backend-only regression after the non-blocking bcrypt change (verify_password_async via asyncio.to_thread). 10/10 pytest cases PASSED against the live preview. All seeded accounts still authenticate (admin/inspector/reviewer on TENANT-000001 and doha.admin on RIYADAH-DOH-001), 401/403 paths return correct codes (no 500s), /me + /refresh round-trip works, and brute-force lockout still trips after 5 fails per {ip,email} bucket. A concurrency probe of 10 parallel admin logins finished in 1.30s wall (median 1.20s per req), confirming bcrypt no longer serialises on the event loop.
test_scope: Backend only. /api/v1/damage-intelligence/auth — login (4 accounts), invalid password, unknown user, /me, /refresh, brute-force lockout (throwaway email), successful login clears counter.

feature_verification.valid_login_doha_admin: PASS - 200, RIYADAH-DOH-001 admin verifies (proves existing $2b$ hashes still verify after the thread-pool wrapping).
feature_verification.invalid_password_401: PASS - 401 with envelope errors[0].message='Invalid email or password.' (NOT 500). Safe message — does not disclose which of email/password was wrong.
feature_verification.unknown_user_401: PASS - 401 for non-existent email; auth.py correctly skips verify_password_async when user is None.
feature_verification.me_with_bearer: PASS - GET /auth/me with Authorization: Bearer <token> + X-Tenant-Id: TENANT-000001 returns the principal with permissions populated.
feature_verification.refresh_round_trip: PASS - POST /auth/refresh returns a new accessToken which successfully authenticates against /me.
feature_verification.brute_force_lockout: PASS - 403 'Too many failed login attempts' observed after >=5 failed attempts into a single {ip,email} bucket. Used a unique throwaway email (lockout.test+<rand>@riyadah.tech) so the real admin/inspector are NOT locked out.
feature_verification.success_clears_counter: PASS - 2 fails on the real admin followed by a successful login -> di_login_attempts cleared; admin can re-login immediately.

concurrency_sanity_check.interpretation: wall ~= per-request latency proves bcrypt is running off the asyncio event loop (asyncio.to_thread) - the change achieves its performance goal. A blocking implementation would have produced wall ~= 10 * per-request.

critical_code_review_comments: application/security/password.py: hash_password_async / verify_password_async correctly wrap the synchronous bcrypt helpers via asyncio.to_thread. The sync variants are retained for the offline admin_seed.py script (which runs outside the event loop) - good separation.

api/routes/auth.py:108-114 short-circuits the bcrypt call when the user is None and reuses the SAME 401 response for both unknown-user and bad-password. This preserves the previous safe-error contract (no user-enumeration via response timing OR message). The thread offload does NOT change the constant-time-like behaviour at the response-layer; if absolute timing-side-channel parity is desired in the future, a dummy verify_password_async() against a fixed hash could be added in the user-is-None branch.

Brute-force lockout identifier is {request.client.host}:{email}. In this kubernetes preview env, ingress rotates upstream requests across ~2 different proxy IPs, so the per-IP bucket fills more slowly than a single-IP client would. Not a regression - same behaviour as before the bcrypt change. If product wants lockout to be tighter behind a load balancer, switch the identifier to use X-Forwarded-For (left-most) instead of request.client.host.
test_credentials: admin@riyadah.tech / DamageAdmin#2026, inspector@riyadah.tech / Inspector#2026, reviewer@riyadah.tech / Reviewer#2026 (all TENANT-000001); doha.admin@riyadah.tech / DohaAdmin#2026 (RIYADAH-DOH-001). All verified working post-change.
seed_data_creation: None. Throwaway lockout emails (lockout.test+<uuid>@riyadah.tech) wrote ephemeral rows into di_login_attempts; these are harmless and will be evicted by _is_locked's stale-window cleanup or can be deleted manually. The real admin's failed-counter was deliberately cleared at the end of every test that produced fails.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Auth post-bcrypt-thread-pool change is fully verified. Login response envelope = {success, data:{accessToken, refreshToken, tokenType:'Bearer', user:{id,email,displayName,tenantId,roles,permissions}}, correlationId, errors:null}. Error envelope = {success:false, errors:[{code, message}], correlationId, data:null} - read messages from body['errors'][0]['message']. /me and /refresh need NO X-Tenant-Id for /refresh but DO need it (plus Bearer) for /me. Lockout identifier per {ip,email} - preview ingress rotates client.host between ~2 IPs (e.g. 10.232.133.130 / 10.232.129.197), so to force a guaranteed 403 in a single test, fire >=10-14 failing attempts into the same throwaway email. Concurrency: 10 parallel admin logins resolve in ~1.3s wall, ~1.2s per request - safe to do parallel auth-bearing tests without serialising on bcrypt.
